Which of these quantities is a vector?\n:
1) A vector needs both magnitude and direction.
2) Velocity is displacement per time, so it has a direction.
Answer: velocity.
Why the others are wrong: mass has size only, so it is a scalar.
Which of these quantities is a scalar?\n:
1) A scalar has magnitude only.
2) Distance is total path length and has no direction.
Answer: distance.
Why the others are wrong: displacement is tempting but it points from start to finish, so it is a vector.
A vector is completely described by its\:
1) A vector must say how much and which way.
Answer: magnitude and direction.
Why the others are wrong: magnitude only describes a scalar.
A runner completes one full lap of a 400:
1) Distance is the path length, 400 m.
2) She ends where she began, so displacement = 0 m.
Answer: 400 m and 0 m.
Why the others are wrong: 400 m and 400 m confuses displacement with distance.
A student walks 6.0 m east and then 8.0:
1) The legs are perpendicular.
2) d = sqrt(6.0^2 + 8.0^2) = sqrt(100) = 10 m.
Answer: 10 m.
Why the others are wrong: 14 m is the distance walked, not the straight-line displacement.
A car has a velocity of -20 m/s. What do:
1) In one dimension the sign gives direction.
2) Negative means opposite the positive axis direction.
Answer: The car moves in the negative direction of the chosen axis.
Why the others are wrong: the sign says nothing about slowing down, and the speeds of +20 and -20 m/s are equal.
Vector A points east with magnitude 5 m/:
1) The negative of a vector keeps the magnitude.
2) It reverses the direction, so east becomes west.
Answer: 5 m/s pointing west.
Why the others are wrong: a magnitude cannot be negative, so -5 m/s east is not a valid description.
A boat travels 40 m east and then 30 m n:
1) tan(theta) = opposite / adjacent = 30 / 40 = 0.75.
2) theta = tan^-1(0.75) = 36.9 degrees, measured from east toward north.
Answer: 37 degrees north of east.
Why the others are wrong: 53 degrees comes from using 40 / 30 and is the angle from north.
A hiker walks 9.0 km east, then 4.0 km w:
1) Distance = 9.0 + 4.0 + 3.0 = 16 km.
2) Displacement with east positive = 9.0 - 4.0 + 3.0 = +8.0 km.
Answer: 16 km and 8.0 km east.
Why the others are wrong: 16 km and 16 km east ignores the westward leg when finding displacement.
A car moves around a circular track at a:
1) Speed is a scalar and stays 20 m/s.
2) Velocity is a vector and its direction keeps changing around the circle.
Answer: Its speed is constant but its velocity is changing.
Why the others are wrong: constant speed does not mean constant velocity.
The resultant of two vectors is\nthe sin:
1) Adding vectors gives one vector that replaces them.
Answer: the single vector with the same effect as the two together.
Why the others are wrong: the resultant is not simply the larger vector.
A 5 m/s east velocity is added to a 3 m/:
1) Same direction, so magnitudes add.
2) 5 + 3 = 8 m/s.
Answer: 8 m/s east.
Why the others are wrong: 2 m/s would be the result for opposite directions.
A 5 N force acts east and a 3 N force ac:
1) Opposite directions, so subtract.
2) 5 - 3 = 2 N in the direction of the larger force, east.
Answer: 2 N east.
Why the others are wrong: 8 N east adds forces that point in opposite directions.
A velocity of 20 m/s points 30 degrees a:
1) The horizontal component uses cosine for an angle from the horizontal.
2) 20 cos(30) = 20 x 0.866 = 17.3 m/s.
Answer: 17.3 m/s.
Why the others are wrong: 10.0 m/s is 20 sin(30), the vertical component.
A 12 N force acts east and a 5.0 N force:
1) The forces are perpendicular.
2) R = sqrt(12^2 + 5.0^2) = sqrt(169) = 13 N.
Answer: 13 N.
Why the others are wrong: 17 N simply adds the magnitudes.
A 50 N force acts 37 degrees above the x:
1) The y component is F sin(theta).
2) 50 x sin(37) = 50 x 0.602 = 30 N.
Answer: 30 N.
Why the others are wrong: 40 N is 50 cos(37), the x component.
When adding vectors tip-to-tail, the res:
1) Place each vector's tail at the previous tip.
2) The resultant closes the path from the start to the end.
Answer: the tail of the first vector to the tip of the last vector.
Why the others are wrong: starting at a tip points the resultant backward.

Answer: 12.2 N.
Why the others are wrong: 14.0 N just adds the magnitudes.
Three forces keep an object in equilibri:
1) The first two combine to sqrt(6.0^2 + 8.0^2) = 10 N toward the northeast.
2) Equilibrium needs a zero total, so the third force is 10 N in the opposite direction, south of west.
Answer: 10 N pointing south of west.

Two vectors have magnitudes 6 and 8. Whi:
1) The resultant is at least 8 - 6 = 2 and at most 8 + 6 = 14.
2) Only 3 lies between 2 and 14.
Answer: 3.
Why the others are wrong: 15 exceeds the maximum of 14.
The velocity of an object relative to an:
1) Velocity depends on the observer's frame.
Answer: its velocity as measured in that observer's frame of reference.
Why the others are wrong: different observers can measure different velocities.
A boat moves at 5.0 m/s in still water a:
1) Downstream the current helps.
2) 5.0 + 2.0 = 7.0 m/s.
Answer: 7.0 m/s.

1) Upstream the current opposes the boat.
2) 5.0 - 2.0 = 3.0 m/s.
Answer: 3.0 m/s.

A passenger walks forward at 1.5 m/s alo:
1) Same direction, so velocities add.
2) 20 + 1.5 = 21.5 m/s.
Answer: 21.5 m/s.
Why the others are wrong: 18.5 m/s would be correct only if she walked toward the back.
A plane has an airspeed of 200 km/h head:
1) A headwind opposes the motion.
2) 200 - 40 = 160 km/h.
Answer: 160 km/h.
Why the others are wrong: 240 km/h would be the result with a tailwind.

2) v = sqrt(4.0^2 + 3.0^2) = sqrt(25) = 5.0 m/s.
Answer: 5.0 m/s.
Why the others are wrong: 7.0 m/s adds perpendicular velocities directly.
A boat aimed straight across a 120 m wid:
1) Only the velocity across the river moves the boat across.
2) t = 120 m / 4.0 m/s = 30 s.
Answer: 30 s.

The boat in the previous situation cross:
1) The current carries the boat for the whole crossing time.
2) drift = 3.0 m/s x 30 s = 90 m.
Answer: 90 m.
Why the others are wrong: 120 m is the river width, not the drift.
Car A moves at 25 m/s east and car B mov:
1) Take east as positive, so vA = +25 and vB = -15.
2) v(AB) = vA - vB = 25 - (-15) = +40 m/s.

A plane heads north with an airspeed of:
1) The air velocity and wind are perpendicular.
2) v = sqrt(150^2 + 50^2) = sqrt(25000) = 158 km/h.

Ignoring air resistance, the horizontal:
1) Gravity acts only downward, so there is no horizontal acceleration.

Answer: 9.8 m/s^2 downward.
Why the others are wrong: the acceleration does not become zero at the top.
One ball rolls off a table horizontally:
1) Vertical motion depends only on height and g.
2) Both start with zero vertical speed, so both fall for the same time.

2) t = sqrt(2 x 19.6 / 9.8) = sqrt(4.0) = 2.0 s.

A ball leaves a table horizontally at 15:
1) Horizontal velocity is constant.
2) x = vx t = 15 x 2.0 = 30 m.

2) vy = g t = 9.8 x 2.0 = 19.6 m/s downward.

A ball thrown horizontally at 12 m/s fal:

2) v = sqrt(12^2 + 19.6^2) = sqrt(528) = 23 m/s.

Two stones are thrown horizontally from:

At the highest point of a projectile's p:
